# massdriver_custom_attribute (Resource)

A custom attribute declared for the organization. Custom attributes are the keys (with a closed set of allowed values) that projects, environments, components, and bundle repositories are tagged with, and that group policy conditions and default tags reference. Deleting a custom attribute does not remove values already set on resources.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "massdriver_custom_attribute" "team" {
  key      = "team"
  scope    = "PROJECT"
  values   = ["platform", "data", "payments"]
  required = true
}

resource "massdriver_custom_attribute" "data_classification" {
  key    = "data_classification"
  scope  = "ENVIRONMENT"
  values = ["public", "internal", "restricted"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `key` (String) Attribute key. 1-64 characters, starting with a letter or underscore and containing only letters, digits, and underscores. Unique within the organization, case-insensitively. Changing it replaces the attribute.
- `scope` (String) Where the attribute is set: `PROJECT`, `ENVIRONMENT`, `COMPONENT`, or `REPO`. Project and environment values cascade to everything beneath them. Changing it replaces the attribute.
- `values` (List of String) The closed set of values the attribute may take. At least one; no duplicates, empty strings, or `*`. Changing the set does not revalidate resources already tagged.

### Optional

- `required` (Boolean) Whether every new resource at `scope` must set this attribute. Defaults to `false` (the platform's own default is `true`). Existing resources are not revalidated.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by key or by ID.
terraform import massdriver_custom_attribute.team team
```
